rules.condition: while the timer is active and incrementing
rules.statement: The prescaler and step fields must be stable for the timer value to increment correctly.

rules.condition: when software wants to change prescaler or step
rules.statement: Software should de-activate the timer before changing the prescaler or step fields, then proceed with the change.
The CPU cannot access a 64-bit value in a single request over the 32-bit register interface; two 32-bit accesses are required.

rules.condition: when a 64-bit timer value is read as two separate 32-bit reads
rules.statement: The timer value may increment between the two 32-bit reads of mtime and mtimeh.

rules.condition: when reading the 64-bit timer value in two reads
rules.statement: A rollover between the two reads can be detected in a standard way using a third read.

rules.condition: when mtime must be set to an arbitrary, dynamically-determined value
rules.statement: Software should use the prescribed safe write sequence to set mtime so timer operation does not yield an indeterminate result.

rules.condition: when the target lower half of mtime is close to 0xFFFF_FFFF
rules.statement: The safe write sequence should be used so the timer does not assume an incorrect time between the two 32-bit writes.
mtimecmp shall be written after mtime in order to clear any pending interrupt condition.

rules.condition: when CFG0.step is above 1 and mtimecmp is close to 0xFFFF_FFFF_FFFF_FFFF
rules.statement: One tick can carry mtime from below mtimecmp past the end of the range, so mtime skips mtimecmp and the interrupt is not raised.

rules.condition: when the computed mtime + timeout comparison value overflows
rules.statement: Software may set mtimecmp to 0xFFFF_FFFF_FFFF_FFFF to get an intermediate interrupt.

rules.condition: in the service routine for the intermediate all-ones interrupt
rules.statement: The service routine needs to poll mtime until it wraps before scheduling the required interrupt with the originally computed mtimecmp value.
mtime can step over the all-ones value so the intermediate interrupt is never raised.
Setting mtimecmp to 0xFFFF_FFFF_FFFF_FFFF - step + 1 works for the intermediate interrupt, since the last mtime before wrap is at least that large.
The interrupt can be cleared by writing 1 to the Interrupt Status register INTR_STATE0.
The interrupt can be cleared by updating mtimecmp; a write to either COMPARE_LOWER0_0 or COMPARE_UPPER0_0 clears the interrupt source.

rules.condition: when mtime is greater than or equal to mtimecmp
rules.statement: The RV_TIMER module generates the interrupt when mtime is greater than or equal to mtimecmp.
